A man peeped through a hole as the Prophet combed his head; had he known, the Prophet said, he would have pierced his eye, as asking permission prevents unlawful looking.
A man peeped into the Prophet's room, and the Prophet said he would have pierced his eye, for asking permission to enter was ordained because of looking.
The Prophet greeted and repeated words three times; whoever asks permission thrice unanswered should leave, as Abu Musa proved to Umar, and the people of Suffa asked before entering.
When Jabir knocked and answered 'I' to the Prophet's 'Who is that?', the Prophet repeated 'I, I?' as if he disliked it.
No blame falls on one who blinds with a stone a man peeping into his house without permission, and the Prophet aimed an arrowhead at a man peeping in.
The Prophet aimed an arrowhead at a man peeping into his house, said asking permission exists to prevent unlawful looks, and one who pokes a peeper's eye is blameless.
Umar found the Prophet in an upper room with a black slave at the top of the stairs, asked through him for permission, and was admitted.
